doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Rachmaninoff's Third Concerto when she is down
summary: She works on the Rachmaninoff Third for its many notes and hears spirituals and jazz themes in his music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Can you tell me something—when you’re really, really down, which one of these do you prefer to play?
I like to work on the Rachmaninoff Third Concerto.
When you’re really down? What does it do for you?
I don’t know, there’s so many notes to play.
You know they say that you receive music sometimes through the crown of your head, sometimes through your throat, sometimes through your solar plexus. Is that what Rachmaninoff does for you?
He does everything. I think some of his music has some Negro spirituals in it.
Especially the Rachmaninoff Third. In some of his music you can hear themes that could be presented as jazz.
